faq.q: When I rotate by a free angle, why does the image get bigger?
faq.a: With 'Expand to fit' selected, the canvas grows so the tilted image is never clipped. The new size comes from the rotated bounding box: width' = |w·cos θ| + |h·sin θ| and height' = |w·sin θ| + |h·cos θ|. For example a 4000×3000 photo rotated 30° becomes about 4964×4598. The triangular corners left over are filled with transparency or a colour you pick. Choose 'Crop to original size' instead if you only want a small straightening tweak and are happy to lose the overflowing edges.

faq.q: Do the 90° and flip buttons reduce quality?
faq.a: No. Rotating by 90°, 180° or 270° and flipping horizontally or vertically are done with an exact canvas transform at full resolution, so every pixel is preserved — these are lossless orientation changes. A 90° turn simply swaps the width and height. Only the free-angle slider resamples pixels, because a non-right-angle rotation has to interpolate; it still works at full resolution with high-quality smoothing.

faq.q: Can I rotate a whole folder of images the same way?
faq.a: Yes. Drop several files and an 'Apply to all & download ZIP' button appears. It runs your exact current operation — the 90° steps, flips, free angle, canvas mode and background — on every image and packs the results into a ZIP built in your browser with JSZip. Files that can't be decoded are skipped and reported rather than failing the whole batch.

faq.q: What happens to corners, format and metadata?
faq.a: For free angles the exposed corners are transparent (keep PNG or WebP to preserve that) or filled with a colour of your choice (needed for JPG, which has no transparency). You can keep the original format or export JPG, PNG or WebP with a quality slider. The canvas re-encode drops EXIF and GPS metadata, and because phone photos are decoded upright first, a rotation is applied on top of the already-correct orientation.
